claims.text: In August 2025 Reps. Deborah Ross (NC), Valerie Foushee (NC) and Morgan McGarvey (KY), past recipients of AIPAC money, said they would not accept further AIPAC donations; Ross had received $41,900 (2022) and $97,876 (2024) from AIPAC, and Foushee more than $800,000 in direct and bundled AIPAC giving plus about $2M in super PAC support in 2022.

A July 2025 Gallup poll found 8% of Democrats approved of Israel's military action in Gaza, down from 36% in November 2023; AIPAC's spokesman said the group would remain engaged in the 2026 elections; Reps. Wesley Bell and Jonathan Jackson said they would keep taking or defending AIPAC support.

Track AIPAC lists at $0 career pro-Israel money Senators Bernie Sanders, Chris Van Hollen, Jeff Merkley and Peter Welch; Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Rashida Tlaib, Ilhan Omar, Summer Lee, Pramila Jayapal, Greg Casar and Ayanna Pressley; and Rep. Thomas Massie.

claims.text: In late July 2025 Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-GA) wrote that the 7 October attack was horrific and hostages must be returned, 'so is the genocide, humanitarian crisis, and starvation happening in Gaza'; Reuters described her as the first Republican lawmaker to call the Gaza crisis a genocide.

The House rejected, 422–6, Greene's amendment to strip $500 million in annual cooperative missile-defense funding for Israel (Iron Dome, Arrow, David's Sling) from the 2026 defense bill; the six votes in favor were Greene, Massie, Omar, Al Green, Summer Lee and Tlaib; Greene called the funding 'money we don't have' and said Israel is 'very capable of defending themselves'.

On 7 August 2025 AIPAC called Greene's genocide accusation 'disgusting' and said 'Marjorie Taylor Greene is the newest member of the anti-Israel Squad'; she replied 'Bring. It. On.' and 'I can't be bought and I'm not backing down!!'

Jewish Insider described Greene as amplifying antisemitic rhetoric, citing among other things her earlier claim that space-based weapons tied to the Rothschild family caused California wildfires, a post saying 'I'll never take 30 shekels', and suggestions that Israel or 'powerful people' might target her; it reported that the Republican Jewish Coalition had endorsed primary challengers to defeat her, and quoted AIPAC's spokesman calling her statements 'rancid anti-Israel and unhinged raving'. It also reported she called for AIPAC and other pro-Israel groups to register as foreign agents and called the ADL a 'dangerous hate group'.

On 14 November 2025 President Trump withdrew his endorsement of Greene on Truth Social, saying he saw her 'complain, complain, complain' and that he would back the 'right candidate' against her in a primary; Greene had broken with the White House on tariffs, foreign policy, inflation and healthcare and had signed the petition to force a House vote on releasing the Epstein files, which she linked to his attack.

Greene announced on 21 November 2025 that she would resign effective 5 January 2026, saying her disagreements 'should not result in me being called a traitor and threatened by the President of the United States', that she would not 'endure a hurtful and hateful primary against me by the President we all fought for', and 'I refuse to be a "battered wife"'; NPR called the Epstein files dispute the final straw and noted her opposition to the Iran strikes and to support for Israel's war in Gaza.

Her resignation letter did not name Israel but spoke of 'foreign interests' and opposition to foreign wars and aid; the RJC responded with a gif captioned 'And we say bye bye', and Rep. Randy Fine posted 'One antisemite down. One to go.'

After Trump called her a 'traitor', Greene posted an image showing $0.00 in AIPAC money next to her name and more than $230 million tied to Trump (Track AIPAC's figure for pro-Israel spending benefiting him since 2020), writing 'I AM AMERICA FIRST'; the DCNF found no public record of direct AIPAC donations to her.
